title: Sort and filter a table
summary: Sort a table by amount and filter it by month, then clear the filter.

steps.say: Make sure your data is a table with arrow buttons in the header row. Say done when you see them.

checks.prompt: Are there filter arrow buttons in the header row of the data?

hints: The arrows sit at the right of each heading cell.
Click inside the data and press Control Shift L to turn the filter buttons on.
steps.why: Sort and filter commands live behind those header arrows.

steps.say: Click the arrow button in the Amount heading.

checks.prompt: Is a dropdown menu open under the Amount heading with sort options?

hints: It is the small arrow at the right edge of cell B1.
Click B1 and press Alt and the down arrow.
steps.why: Each column has its own sort and filter menu.

checks.prompt: Are the rows now ordered with the biggest Amount at the top?

hints: It is the second option at the top of the menu.
Use the Data tab and click the Z to A sort button instead.
steps.why: Sorting puts the biggest values where you see them first.

steps.say: Now click the arrow button in the Month heading.

checks.prompt: Is a dropdown menu open under the Month heading with a list of months?

hints: It is at the right edge of cell A1.
Click A1 and press Alt and the down arrow.
steps.why: Filtering hides rows you don't need right now.

steps.say: Untick Select All, tick two months, then click OK.

checks.prompt: Does the table now show only two month rows, with a funnel icon on the Month heading?

hints: The month list is in the lower half of the menu. OK is at the bottom.
Type a month name in the Search box to find it quickly.
steps.why: Hidden rows are still there, only out of sight.

steps.say: Open the Month arrow again and click Clear Filter From Month to show every row.

checks.prompt: Are all six month rows visible again?

hints: The funnel icon on the heading shows a filter is active.
On the Data tab, click Clear in the Sort and Filter group.
steps.why: Clearing filters avoids thinking data went missing.
